identity.title: CON-quest. Searching for the most obscured galaxy nuclei

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the first results of a systematic survey of infrared luminous galaxies, called CON-quest, with the aim to search for compact obscured nuclei, traced by strong HCN-vib emission.

question.value: How common are CONs in the local Universe, and does their prevalence depend on host luminosity or other properties?

evidence.quote: We aim to establish how common CONs are in the local Universe ($z<0.08$), and whether their prevalence depends on the luminosity or other properties of the host galaxy.

referee_caveats_inferred: The supplied sample table has lost its target-name column; assigning its coordinates and distances to named galaxies would require inference.
The supplied results table has numbered literature references but no mapping, blocking source-specific archival provenance.
Several CON surface brightnesses have large uncertainties or lie close to the empirical boundary; classification uncertainty is not propagated explicitly into prevalence.
A nonsignificant inclination test does not establish equal distributions or exclude a nuclear-orientation effect.
The continuum correlation should be checked against shared-area covariance and detection selection.
Mixing 3-2 observations with three 4-3 nondetections needs an explicit sensitivity-equivalence justification.
Tentative flow signatures do not uniquely establish inflow/outflow geometry or causality.
